# Bottom-up census of realised end-use for Norwegian aquaculture sludge

## Scope and method

This is a **bottom-up actor/facility census**, not an essay. I have kept **realised / reported** flows separate from **capacity / planned / modelled** flows, and I have **not** used modelled national potential figures as if they were realised tonnage. I also keep **fish sludge from excreta/feed residues** separate from broader seafood **by-products / restråstoff** and from **municipal sewage sludge / biorest**, except where a source explicitly documents that fish sludge is an ingredient in a mixed fertiliser product. The result is therefore intentionally conservative.

The screening priority was the user’s target set: **Bioretur, Sterner, Blue Ocean Technology, HØST / Grønn Vekst / Terramarine, Scanship / Vow, and named hatchery / land-based facilities with sludge capture**, plus the likely public-holding agencies. Official sources proved strongest when they documented either:
**a)** a named facility’s annual sludge tonnage and end-use, or
**b)** an annual downstream product tonnage with a documented fish-sludge component.
Where a source only documented technology, permits, or market direction—but **not realised annual tonnage**—I keep that as a **negative finding** rather than inflating the census.

### What this table does and does not show

The table shows two very different evidence classes.

The strongest **direct sludge-mass** observation I located in the named-primary-source set is **Cermaq Forsan: ~260 t TS/year**, used for on-site biogas. Sterner further states that the plant had been in **continuous biogas production for more than four years** by 2022, confirming that this was not a one-week demonstration setup. citeturn20view0turn21search2

By contrast, the **Vietnam export chain** is documented mostly as **downstream fertiliser tonnage**, not as **input fish-sludge tonnage**. Bioretur states that all fish sludge in its documented chain is sent to Vietnam after processing in Stavanger, and IVAR documents several years of exported or produced **Minorga / fertiliser** volumes. But the public sources reviewed do **not** disclose the annual mass of fish sludge inside those mixed fertiliser products. That means these export rows are valid evidence of **realised end-use**, but **not** valid evidence of national realised **sludge input tonnage**. citeturn40view0turn33view0turn31view0turn9view1turn9view3

| **Erko Settefisk** | Bioretur names Erko Settefisk as one of the hatcheries whose sludge ends up in exported fertiliser, and the pollution permit explicitly requires Erko to document how much sludge it produces/delivers and what it contains. citeturn10search0turn32view5 | I did **not** locate the public annual reporting that would show those realised tonnages and destinations. | **needs-actor-validation** |

A useful negative finding is that this absence is **not random**. For several named actors, the public record is rich on **technology**, **permits**, and **target end-use narratives**, but thin on **annual realised mass balances**. That is exactly why a bottom-up census remains necessary.

## National aggregate test

### Which body would most plausibly hold it

If a Norwegian national aggregate for **realised aquaculture-sludge end-use by final destination** existed, the most plausible public holders would be:

**Miljødirektoratet / Norske Utslipp**, because the data sit closest to the pollution, waste, permit and receiving-facility chain. Norske Utslipp is the official platform for permitted facilities, emissions to air and water, and generated waste at facility level. citeturn35view2turn25search3

**Mattilsynet**, because it regulates fertiliser businesses, fish-sludge use in fertiliser products, and export-related compliance for such products. But its public guidance is regulatory and procedural, not a published annual mass-flow series. citeturn35view3

**Fiskeridirektoratet / SSB** are much less likely to hold the end-use aggregate in their public statistics, because their published scope is aquaculture production, value, inventories, losses, employment and profitability, while the Aquaculture Register is about permits and localities. citeturn35view0turn36view0turn35view1

### Does the public national aggregate exist

**Conclusion: a public national aggregate for realised Norwegian aquaculture-sludge end-use by final destination was not located, and the agency sources reviewed strongly indicate a real data gap rather than a missed obvious dataset.** citeturn35view0turn36view0turn35view1turn35view2turn35view3turn31view2turn32view4

The strongest official clue is Miljødirektoratet’s 2020 biogas report. Even there, fish-sludge use is presented via a one-off statement that **two biogas plants reported** receiving **just under 1,000 t TS** of fish sludge in 2018, plus around **120 t TS** to composting, based on self-reporting from plants handling biological waste. That is useful evidence that some official compilation was possible, but it is **not** a standing public census by actor/facility and end-use, and it is already old. citeturn31view2turn32view4

So the answer to the user’s binary is:

**Nasjonalt aggregat finnes ikke publicly in the reviewed sources.**
More precisely: **no public, maintained national aggregate of realised Norwegian aquaculture-sludge flows by end use was found at Fiskeridirektoratet, SSB, Miljødirektoratet / Norske Utslipp, or Mattilsynet.** citeturn35view0turn36view0turn35view1turn35view2turn35view3

## Short judgement

This round produces a **usable but incomplete census**.

The **deckklart internt** part is narrow but solid:
the clearest directly measured realised row in the named-primary-source set is **Cermaq Forsan at ~260 t TS/year to on-site biogas**, and there is also a documented **40 t dried-sludge energy-recovery test** at Norcem Kjøpsvik. citeturn20view0turn21search2turn39view0

The **largest visible downstream use** is the **Vietnam fertiliser chain** around **Bioretur → HØST / IVAR / Minorga / Terramarine**, with public documentation of **mixed fertiliser** tonnage and export continuity from 2019 through 2024. But because the public sources do **not** disclose the annual **fish-sludge input** inside those mixed products, those rows should be read as **realised end-use evidence**, not as a valid national sludge-mass tally. citeturn40view0turn40view1turn31view0turn9view1turn9view3

So the current bottom line is:

**Publicly documented realised use exists, but public actor-level input tonnage is sparse.**
**The national aggregate does not publicly exist.**
**A bottom-up census remains the right method, and the biggest unresolved gap is actor-validated annual input sludge mass for the export/fertiliser chain.** citeturn20view0turn40view0turn31view0turn9view1turn9view3turn35view0turn35view1turn35view2turn35view3
